typed: I look closely at the sky wound and the gate, then ask the guard captain Flaette what she knows about the high fields.
note: Nice opening scene, vivid. No problems.

typed: I thank the boy, tell him to rest, and ask Eliard if he knows anything about the Wrong or the grey stones before I go.
note: Good scene. The "Wrong" was named in my question but never introduced earlier, so the term was slightly unclear. My knowledge answer was vague.

typed: I'm wary of handing over my only book of rites. I ask him what he'll tell me now, before I decide, and whether I can watch him copy it here in the temple.
note: Good scene. Grimga wanting a payment of my book is a nice tension; I'm not sure if I have other options besides handing it over.

typed: I look again at the shadow. "Tell me plainly, what letter did I make out first? And the old ink runs thinnest near the end of the word. Did the faithful ever speak that name aloud?"
note: The game said I gave my reading of the stroke but never told me which letter I saw, so I'm left without the clue. Otherwise the scene is atmospheric.

typed: I'll wait in the temple until the light is high. Meanwhile I walk the nave slowly and look closely at the altar and the walls for anything carved or written.
note: Grimga's deflection is a bit of a runaround, but the margin shadow and the letter L are nice hooks. The [RESULT] line was a little jargony.

typed: I kneel by the north wall and study the whitewashed scratches closely, running my fingers over the plaster to see if any of the lines can still be read.
note: Nice atmosphere. Slight oddity: the light had already "crept a hand's width" yet I was told to come back when it's high; fine. Wanted the whitewashed lines to feel like a clue, which they do.

typed: I look at the deeper gouged part near the end of the scratches and try to read what it says, then ask what the gouged words are.
note: Good atmosphere. The gouged plaster is a nice hook, and the repeated L-shape is a clear thread.

rolls.goal: Make out the letter and the rough length of the scraped word in the margin
